statement.p: Find the area under the curve y = {\cos(t)\over\sin(t)} between t = 0 and t = \pi/2. Enter diverges if the area is not bounded.

static.solution:
\int_0^{\pi/2}\,{\cos(t)\over\sin(t)}\,dt. However, the integrand is undefined at t = 0, so this is an improper integral. We find \int_0^{\pi/2}\,{\cos(t)\over\sin(t)}\,dt = \lim\limits_{a\to0^{+}}\,\int_a^{\pi/2}\,{\cos(t)\over\sin(t)}\,dt = \lim\limits_{a\to0^{+}}\,(\ln|\sin(t)|)\bigg|_a^{\pi/2} = \lim\limits_{a\to0^{+}} ( \ln(1) - \ln|\sin(a)| ). However, -\ln|\sin(a)| is undefined as a\to0, so this integral diverges.
Thus, because the integral diverges, the area is not bounded.
